newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to hold Mideast economic summit on time.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to hold Mideast economic summit on time.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday his country would hold on time a summit aimed at integrating Israel into the Middle East economy despite last week's bloody clashes between Israelis and Palestinians.

"We are going to hold the economic summit. It is in our benefit to hold the summit. Those countries that want to come are welcome and those who don't, well it's their business. We're saying that the summit is on," Mubarak told reporters.

Fifty-seven Palestinians and 15 Israelis have died in four days of clashes that erupted after Israel opened an archeological tunnel near Islam's third holiest shrine, the al-Aqsa mosque in Arab East Jerusalem.

Mubarak said he was staying away from an emergency Middle East peace summit in Washington to discuss last week's violence because he was displeased with Israel's attitude and actions towards the Palestinians.
Egypt has linked the fate of the summit to progress towards Middle East peace. Mubarak has said he is keen to hold the summit but the atmosphere must be right.

The conference, which follows similar gatherings in Casablanca in 1994 and Amman in 1995, is meant to take place from November 12 to 14, with 85 states and more than 25 international organisations taking part.
